explanation: For three lengths to close into a triangle, the third side c must be longer than the difference of the other two and shorter than their sum: |a - b| < c < a + b. This holds because the shortest path between two points is the straight segment, so going from one base endpoint to the apex and back can never be shorter than the base (giving the upper bound) nor can the base be shorter than the difference of the two slanted sides (the lower bound). The green band on the number line marks that valid window for fixed a and b, and the moving dot is c sweeping in and out of it; when the dot is inside, the triangle closes, and when it leaves, the two sides collapse into a flat hinge that cannot meet.
bullets: The green band on the number line is the only window where c yields a real triangle.
Lower bound |a-b|: the two sides barely differ enough to span c.
Upper bound a+b: at c = a+b the triangle flattens into a straight line.
Outside the window the two sides become a hinge that cannot close.
